content.title: About
content.content: Yellow summer squash (Cucurbita pepo) is a tender, mildly sweet vegetable harvested while still young and soft. Raw squash has a crisp texture, bright yellow color, and a subtly tangy flavor. It is commonly used in salads, marinades, and fresh dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yellow summer squash belongs to the cucurbit family and is a close relative of green summer squash.
The yellow variety contains higher levels of carotenoids, which give it its vivid hue.
Both the skin and seeds are edible, so the whole fruit can be consumed.
In Japan, young squash are often served as tempura, coated in a light rice‑flour batter.
Raw squash is about 95 % water, making it a very low‑calorie food.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Raw yellow squash provides roughly 16 kcal per 100 g, ideal for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids such as beta‑carotene and lutein protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to cucurbit vegetables.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic squash, rinse thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Raw squash can harbor bacteria if stored improperly; keep it refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice raw yellow squash into thin ribbons, matchsticks, or cubes and add to salads, vegetarian rolls, or use as low‑carb “noodle” substitutes. Lightly salting and letting it sit for 10‑15 minutes can draw out excess moisture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store squash in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a container with ventilation at 0‑4 °C. Properly stored, it stays fresh for up to 5 days. Remove any bruised or damaged portions to prevent spoilage of the rest.
